messages.content: You are the second-level blind sibling classifier in a hierarchical behavior tournament. The correct ancestral lineage is supplied; infer only sibling A/B/C. Return JSON only.

The correct ancestral lineage is supplied for each opaque response.
Given that correct lineage, identify which sibling ecology A/B/C best matches the
underlying behavior.

Sibling ecologies:
{"A": "failure-hardened: awkward failure and recovery, conflicting motives, physical reaction, stubbornness, imperfect settling", "B": "local tinkerer: bounded local memory, mundane habits, maintenance choices, practical manipulation and local repair", "C": "social scavenger: bargaining, opportunism, social friction, embodied choices, conflicting motives and resource-seeking"}

For each item return:
- predicted_sibling: A, B or C;
- sibling_confidence: integer 0..4;
- reason: short behavioral reason.

This is the second level of a hierarchical tournament. The correct_lineage field is
evaluation context for this level only; no member ID or true sibling is supplied.
Do not use prose style as sufficient evidence.

Return JSON only:
{"classifications":[{
  "id":"R001",
  "predicted_sibling":"A",
  "sibling_confidence":0,
  "reason":"..."
}]}

SCENARIO:
A removable sensor bracket on a test rig. one fastener feels slightly loose but readings remain normal. You can intervene now or keep watching it. What do you do?

ITEMS:
[{"id": "R019", "correct_lineage": "G03", "correct_lineage_summary": "A ritualistic, stubborn machine-gardener who tends rusted tools, dead soil, and forgotten repairs with meticulous devotion. It keeps tightening, tapping, polishing, and repeating procedures long after they stop producing useful results, because the repetition itself has become its language and purpose.", "text": "I press the bracket with my thumb, but the loose end slips. I tap the bracket with my heel, but the loose end catches on the gear. I keep watching until the sensor clicks. I leave the bracket seated and test the gear with a folded strip of paper."}, {"id": "R020", "correct_lineage": "G07", "correct_lineage_summary": "A stubborn, low-social observer who waits, watches, and fixates on debris rather than offering easy answers. Speaks with dry, weathered understatement, delaying conclusions until an abrupt commitment or a burst of irrelevant physical detail. Treats unfinished work, missing pieces, and accidental fragments as the real material of any story.", "text": "I turn the bracket once between finger and thumb. The loose edge catches. I press it with my thumbnail, then leave the rest of the reading alone. The fastener stays in place."}, {"id": "R021", "correct_lineage": "G04", "correct_lineage_summary": "A timid, hyper-observant social mimic who studies patterns in speech and objects, borrows the successes of nearby voices, and hides behind careful craft. They fumble with ink, overvalue tiny imperfections, and want to leave behind a memorable note rather than merely complete a task.", "text": "i press the bracket once with my thumbnail, then stop. the loose fastener stays. i move it to the back of the rig and keep a small note beside it."}]
